problem_statement: Residents in underserved communities fail to get sanitation hazards (overflowing drains, garbage accumulation) resolved because municipal systems prioritize formal, written, and categorized grievances, ignoring unstructured photo- and voice-based reports.
brief_idea: SanitiSense AI is an AI-powered system that enables low-literacy citizens to report sanitation hazards using a photo and an optional voice note
The system verifies the issue using computer vision
Extracts contextual urgency from voice input
Converts informal citizen reports into structured, evidence-backed civic tickets that authorities can act upon
core_philosophy: Instead of creating another complaint portal, the solution acts as an intelligent translation layer between citizen reality and municipal systems.
usp_points: AI filters spam and invalid submissions automatically
Converts vernacular, unstructured inputs into structured civic data
Aggregates repeated issues to expose ignored sanitation hotspots
solution_steps: Citizens submit a photo of a sanitation issue (mandatory)
Optional voice note provides context such as duration, smell, or obstruction
AI validates whether the image represents a real sanitation hazard
The system classifies issue type and estimates severity
Structured and prioritized sanitation tickets are generated automatically
Repeated complaints are clustered to identify high-risk zones

image_processing: Image-based sanitation issue detection and validation
Automatic spam and irrelevant image rejection
Severity estimation using visual cues (scale, spread, obstruction)
voice_analytics: Voice-based context capture in local languages
Clustering of repeated complaints into sanitation hotspots
Evidence-backed dashboard for authorities or NGOs

technologies: Computer Vision for sanitation image classification
Speech-to-Text for local language voice input
Natural Language Processing for context extraction
Rule-based + lightweight ML models for severity scoring
expected_impact: Increased acknowledgment of valid sanitation complaints
Faster response to high-severity sanitation hazards
Reduced repeat complaints from the same areas
